nodes.label: PQI — Polymarket Qualitative Intelligence
nodes.rationale: Identify mispriced odds in Polymarket event-driven prediction markets via a 7-agent LLM council; default Advisor mode keeps a human in the trade decision loop.

nodes.label: The Council of Seven
nodes.rationale: Seven deliberately biased personas deliberate in parallel (never sequentially, no agent-to-agent talk) — disagreement is the point; flattening the biases is a regression.

nodes.label: The Rules Lawyer
nodes.rationale: Resolution criteria only; receives resolution_criteria injected first as source of truth overriding all other context; 2x weight.

nodes.label: The Bear (Underdog's Advocate)
nodes.rationale: The only structurally independent agent in the mirror-collapse diagnostics; preserving its independence is an explicit Phase 1 guard rail.

nodes.label: Confidence-Weighted Two-Sided Scoring
nodes.rationale: YES and NO scores are independent confidence-weighted averages; gate order price-floor → ceiling → contrarian → market-aligned → EV gate is a stability invariant.

nodes.label: Banded EV Gate
nodes.rationale: Runs last, only converts BUYs to PASS; band-specific Beta-binomial smoothed win rates (BAND_SHRINKAGE_K=5) replaced the scalar PerceivedTrueWinRate in session 31; dormant below MIN_WIN_RATE_SAMPLES to avoid fabricating statistical power.

nodes.label: Kelly Sizing (Half-Kelly Advisory)
nodes.rationale: Half-Kelly (KELLY_MULTIPLIER=0.5) absorbs per-band estimation noise; Kelly inputs must match the gate's banded inputs.

nodes.label: Two-Sidedness Is Autonomy, Not Algebra
nodes.rationale: YES and NO sides are autonomous signals: prices live on independent orderbooks (don't sum to 1 due to spread/vig), per-side confidences carry independent evidence weight; single probability field is a modeling simplification, not algebraic coupling.

nodes.label: Option B Shadow Layer
nodes.rationale: probability_yes/probability_no/probability_source persisted descriptively since session 26; scoring still aggregates the single probability field — step 5 blocked on signal quality, not sample count.

nodes.label: V2 Shared Preamble (PERSONA_V2_PREAMBLE)
nodes.rationale: Phase 1 stage-1 A/B lever live since session 41; must not be edited mid-measurement because content drift invalidates the tagged v2:preamble population.

nodes.label: Phase 0 — Edge Validation
nodes.rationale: Verdict inconclusive: council Brier 0.2176 beats 0.25 chance baseline by ~3pp, mean pre-event CLV −0.0167, realized April PnL −0.575/share; explicitly no knob changes to avoid overfitting on the rows that produced band_stats.

nodes.label: Phase 1 — Signal Quality (Autonomy Fix)
nodes.rationale: Highest-leverage move per the Phase 0 verdict: the aggregate is fragile because 5 of 7 agents mirror each other; fix SHARED_PREAMBLE autonomy framing before any Option B backtest.

nodes.label: LLM Client Contract (pqi/llm/client.py chat())
nodes.rationale: Single chat() entrypoint; LLM_BACKEND env swaps Ollama vs Anthropic; never import anthropic/ollama elsewhere so retry, caching, and kill switches stay centralized.

nodes.label: Centralized Anthropic Retry
nodes.rationale: SDK auto-retry disabled so _chat_anthropic owns the exponential-backoff schedule end-to-end; retryable 5xx incl. 529, 429, connection/timeout; non-retryable 4xx escapes immediately.

nodes.label: Squad Market-Value Enrichment (Transfermarkt)
nodes.rationale: Session 49 ingestion-only track: one descriptive key_context line (squad-value imbalance as a noisy strength proxy) for soccer national-team fixtures; never feeds scoring; non-fatal; public test instance is fragile — Phase 2 moves to dataset-primary.

nodes.label: Live-Event Grace (LIVE_EVENT_GRACE_HOURS)
nodes.rationale: Polymarket stamps soccer endDate at kickoff (esports at kickoff+6h), so the server-side end_date_min=now filter silently dropped in-progress soccer; --live/--starts-within relax end_date_min by 3.0h sized to a match's real max length.

nodes.label: Structured-Match Resolver (Provider Adapter Layer)
nodes.rationale: PandaScoreProvider (esports) + FootballDataProvider (soccer) behind one StructuredMatchProvider interface; non-fatal contract — any failure yields structured_match=None and the pipeline continues.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Stage-1 Monitor
nodes.source_location: PRIORITY — one more monitor pass, then expect to revert
nodes.rationale: 0 of 4 criteria pass at n=78 (cluster fraction pinned at 71%, Bear Brier drifting away from 0.22, council Brier regressed) but the pre-registered decision rule requires n ≥ 100 — flipping at n=78 would look like moving the goalposts, so the revert must be rule-driven, not discretionary.

nodes.label: Four Unified Acceptance Criteria
nodes.source_location: Four unified acceptance criteria (Option B step 5 unblock)
nodes.rationale: All four must pass simultaneously on v2:preamble vs v1: cluster r≥0.85 fraction < 0.50, |drift| > 0.10 on ≥2 agents, Bear Brier toward 0.22 with independence held, council Brier holds/improves from 0.2176.

nodes.label: CTO Agent Reviewer Persona
nodes.rationale: Guardian of edge, math, and architectural purity; four review modes in priority order: quantitative validation, edge assessment, architectural judgment, code/contract review — most mistakes come from letting mode 4 dominate.

nodes.label: Edge First, Scale Second
nodes.rationale: A fast pipeline with no alpha is expensive telemetry; validate edge on held-out data before approving infrastructure migrations.

nodes.label: Parallel Is Not Diverse
nodes.rationale: Running N agents concurrently does not guarantee N independent signals — diversity is a measurement (pairwise correlation, Brier, drift), not an assertion.

nodes.label: Mirror Collapse
nodes.rationale: A signal-quality bug, not a sample-count bug: when agents converge to |drift| ≈ 0 you have one signal wearing seven hats; only prompt/evidence-structure/retrieval-diversity changes help, not more data.

nodes.label: Pre-Event CLV
nodes.rationale: Polymarket has no mid-price close; price at event start vs entry price measures prediction edge independently of the eventual winner, capturable retroactively from CLOB hourly history.

nodes.label: Max Favorable Excursion (MFE)
nodes.rationale: Highest price a position traded at before resolution — the opportunity cost of not taking profit; capturing it as realized PnL requires a continuous listener since Polymarket has no native stop-loss/bracket orders.

nodes.label: Capacity as Third Edge Axis
nodes.rationale: Prediction and execution edge are meaningless above the bankroll where Kelly-sized stakes cannot fill without eating the spread; Tier 2/3 eSports markets often have <$500 depth.

nodes.label: Gate Ordering Invariant
nodes.rationale: price-floor → price-ceiling → contrarian → market-aligned → EV gate; EV gate runs last and only converts BUYs to PASS, never creates a BUY.

nodes.label: Monolith-First, Containers Later
nodes.rationale: The pqi package is already a modular monolith with clean boundaries; containers become valuable only on measured triggers (divergent deploy targets, isolation needs, measured hot-path scaling).

nodes.label: DuckDB Views (history / verdicts / clv_by_row)
nodes.rationale: Ad-hoc SQL over history.jsonl kills the 'every metric needs a Python script' tax.

nodes.label: clv_by_row View (Pre-Event CLV Sidecar)
nodes.rationale: Bucket policy is last-before-event-start to avoid pulling the post-event bucket, which contains resolution-side information.

nodes.label: Reliability Diagram Script
nodes.rationale: Operates over every non-legacy resolved row (~400) rather than only the 65 BUY-triggered ones, using directional-winner semantics — one to two orders of magnitude more data-dense than the BUY subset.

nodes.label: Polymarket CLOB API
nodes.rationale: Read-only price history, no auth; YES and NO tokens fetched in parallel because their prices do not sum to 1.0 (spread/vig).

nodes.label: PandaScore API
nodes.rationale: Symmetric fuzzy scoring min(token_set_ratio_a, token_set_ratio_b) so a perfect match on one side cannot rescue a poor match on the other; non-fatal contract.

nodes.label: Tavily Search API
nodes.rationale: An LLM Search Architect designs category/timing-aware queries before searching, with hardcoded fallback templates if the LLM call fails.

nodes.label: history equity Command
nodes.rationale: Kelly mode is walk-forward: it reads the kelly_stake_scaled fraction frozen on each CouncilResult at analysis time, so there is no look-ahead.

nodes.label: Batch Mode (Multi-Select Analyze)
nodes.rationale: Persistence runs sequentially after the batch because JSONL appends larger than PIPE_BUF aren't safe to interleave; failures isolated per row.

nodes.label: CTO Review: eSports Predictive Engine v2.0
nodes.rationale: Verdict: approve PostgreSQL, async, evaluation framework, LLM centralization; delay microservices, multi-model MoE, heavy orchestration — prove the edge before scaling complexity.

nodes.label: eSports Predictive Engine v2.0 Proposal
nodes.rationale: Proposes migrating the monolith to Dockerized microservices (Scout, Resolver, Historian, Journalist, Syndicate, Bookie) with PostgreSQL, Airflow/Prefect, and Redis, justified by five claimed bottlenecks.

nodes.label: 68% Win Rate Claim
nodes.rationale: Unverified premise the CTO review demands be validated: out-of-sample? sample size? Sharpe/drawdown? CLV? A WR with no denominator is a vibe, not a measurement.

nodes.label: Model Mixing for Divergence
nodes.rationale: Proposed to break correlated base-model bias by running different foundation models per agent; the CTO stance is that vendor diversity is not evidence of independence — it must be measured.

nodes.label: Ghost Events (Gamma Indexing Bug)
nodes.rationale: Events fetchable by direct ID but invisible to all list queries; no client-side workaround exists — possibly related to mid-match settlement de-indexing.

nodes.label: Two-Sided Confidence Asymmetry (Open Question)
nodes.rationale: A high-confidence 'Team A almost certainly loses' is stronger signal than its low-confidence algebraic mirror; symmetric feeding into scoring probably leaves information on the table — deferred until enough resolved samples exist to backtest.

nodes.label: 529 vs 429 Distinction
nodes.rationale: 429 means we exceeded our quota and should slow down; 529 means Anthropic is shedding load and only patience helps — both retryable but with different usage implications.

nodes.label: Option B — Per-Side Probability Autonomy
nodes.rationale: A.1 Option A probability transforms all failed pre-registered acceptance on train and holdout — the confidence-asymmetry signal at the aggregate level is too weak to extract by transformation, so the next lever is changing what agents emit upstream (independent probability_yes / probability_no).

nodes.label: Synthetic Mirror Backfill
nodes.rationale: Do not re-run agents on historical rows: personas have evolved, so re-runs would produce a different council than the one that scored the markets. Instead add probability_no = 1 − probability tagged synthetic_mirror — zero API cost, preserves every existing resolution-based metric exactly.

nodes.label: probability_source Flag
nodes.rationale: Per-verdict (not per-row) flag so partially re-run rows can mix synthetic and independent verdicts; all Option-B-specific analytics must filter on probability_source == independent.

nodes.label: Pre-Registered B-Math Acceptance Criteria
nodes.rationale: Identical in spirit to A.1 β and documented up front so goalposts can't move: Brier Δ ≤ −0.005 on both train and holdout, bootstrap 95% CI entirely below 0, thresholds pre-committed before the first run.

nodes.label: Coherence Metric |p_yes + p_no − 1|
nodes.rationale: Mechanically zero today; under Option B a non-zero value is real signal (genuine uncertainty or non-mirror sides). Parser stays lenient because forcing coherence would destroy the very signal being extracted.

nodes.label: Dempster-Shafer Explicit Ignorance
nodes.rationale: Model the 1 − max(c_yes, c_no) slice as 'I don't know' rather than forcing it onto a side; proper belief combination only becomes possible once per-side probabilities are first-class.

nodes.label: Phase 1 Acceptance Criteria Patch
nodes.rationale: Reconciles Phase 1's original per-agent YES/NO drift criteria (pre-Phase-0) with the Phase 0 retrospective's cluster-collapse + Bear miscalibration finding, so the SHARED_PREAMBLE rewrite targets both pathologies instead of one.

nodes.label: Unified Four-Criterion Acceptance
nodes.rationale: All four criteria (cluster-pair r>=0.85 fraction <0.50; |drift|>0.10 on >=2 agents; Bear Brier toward 0.22 with independence preserved; council Brier holds/improves from 0.2176) must pass simultaneously — a rewrite fixing one while regressing another is not acceptance.

nodes.label: Persona-Specific Evidence Anchoring (Mechanism 2)
nodes.rationale: Cluster collapse arises because agents reason over the same narrative substrate; forcing each persona's reasoning chain through persona-specific ground (base-rate, meta detail, crowd signal, disruption vector) decorrelates outputs at the source rather than at the aggregator.

nodes.label: Bear Probability-After-Advocacy (Mechanism 3)
nodes.rationale: Bear's Brier 0.2810 comes from producing probabilities as an expression of its advocacy role; forcing probability output after the advocacy case (advocate first, then estimate honestly) fixes calibration without destroying Bear's structural independence.

nodes.label: agent_weights.json Reset Before Rollout
nodes.rationale: Weights from the pre-rewrite period partly absorb Bear miscalibration; preserving them would anchor the aggregator to the pathology the rewrite removes (external review v2 §3.4/§5.8).

nodes.label: Phase Dependency Graph
nodes.rationale: P0→P1→P2a; P0→P2b→P2c; P3 after P0; P4 reactive. P2a blocks on P1 (signal trust) not P2b (exit discipline); P1+P2b parallelize because they touch different files.

nodes.label: Anti-Goals (Explicit Rejections)
nodes.rationale: Microservices, Postgres, Redis, Airflow, day-one multi-model MoE, cloud migration, and pre-gate auto-trading are rejected; resurfacing one without a Phase 4 trigger firing is a Technical Debt Alert.

nodes.norm_label: phase 1: signal quality fix (option b autonomy)

nodes.label: Mirror Collapse
nodes.rationale: Agents reason as if YES and NO are algebraic mirrors (per-agent |drift| 0.01–0.06), making the Option B ΔBrier acceptance criterion mathematically unreachable. A signal-quality bug, not a sample-count bug — more data will not help.

nodes.label: Cluster Collapse
nodes.rationale: 5-agent correlated cluster (rules_lawyer/statistician/sentiment/specialist/contrarian at r 0.80–0.92) means the council has ~3 effective voices, not 7.

nodes.label: Task 1.1 SHARED_PREAMBLE Autonomy Rewrite
nodes.rationale: Three complementary mechanisms: asymmetric evidence mechanics (mirror collapse), persona-specific anchoring (cluster collapse), Bear probability-after-advocacy (Bear calibration). Anchors are first-draft direction, not settled text.

nodes.label: Task 1.2 Persona-by-Persona Rollout
nodes.rationale: Single-shot preamble rewrite has too many simultaneous constraints; roll out rules_lawyer→statistician→sentiment→specialist→contrarian→bull→bear, measuring drift between stages. Bull/Bear last because they are most mirror-collapse-prone.

nodes.label: Task 1.3 Pairwise Diversity Measurement
nodes.rationale: |drift| is the individual-agent metric; pairwise Pearson is the cross-agent diversity metric — both must move. Pearson (not Spearman) keeps apples-to-apples with the retro §5.3 baseline. scripts/agent_pairwise_diversity.py.

nodes.label: Task 1.4 Option B Backtest (Conditional)
nodes.rationale: Only worth running after all four unified criteria pass — running the pre-registered backtest on a still-collapsed signal is pre-registered to fail.

nodes.label: Stage 1 Monitor (PERSONA_V2_PREAMBLE)
nodes.rationale: V2 preamble live since session 41; monitor passes at n=38 (1/4) and n=78 (0/4) show cluster fraction moved the wrong way (43%→71%, Bull collapsed into cluster); verdict deferred until n>=100, expected revert.

nodes.label: Phase 2a: Tier A Auto-BUY
nodes.rationale: Tier A automates entry only and holds to resolution — it needs the council signal to be trustworthy (Phase 1) but not MFE validation; splitting it from the old execution-edge bundle keeps the critical path clean.

nodes.label: pqi buy Command
nodes.rationale: Narrowest possible Tier A surface: one market, one decision, no continuous state. Kelly-sized stake from kelly_stake_scaled, structured logging to fills.jsonl.

nodes.label: Idempotency Guard
nodes.rationale: Hash (market_id, analysis_run_id) into a deterministic key; refuse a second fill for the same pair so retriggered analyses cannot double-fill.

nodes.label: Pre-Trade Price Drift Abort
nodes.rationale: Kelly stake and ROI were priced at analyze-time; if top-of-book moved more than TIER_A_PRICE_DRIFT_ABORT_PCT (3%) the assumptions are invalid — abort rather than fill.

nodes.label: Ghost-Event ID-Based Probing
nodes.rationale: Gamma list endpoints intermittently drop events; probe /events/{id} individually before deciding an event is gone. Optional insurance for Tier A, mandatory for Tier B position monitoring.

nodes.label: First-10-Fills Checklist
nodes.rationale: Manual operator gate: first 10 fills reviewed by hand before --unattended is acceptable; live trading has surprise modes (broker rejects, partial fills, slippage) that are cheap to catch on a canary sample.

nodes.label: Phase 2b: MFE Analysis
nodes.rationale: Polymarket has no native stop-loss/take-profit; before building a listener, measure whether MFE on historical BUYs is large enough after fees and slippage to be worth capturing at all.

nodes.label: Max Favorable Excursion (MFE)
nodes.rationale: max(price) - entry_price between entry and resolution — the exit-edge leg of the CTO-§5 triangulation. Retroactive hourly-CLOB MFE is a lower bound on realtime MFE.

nodes.label: Chronological Train/Test Split
nodes.rationale: Best-in-sample TP threshold is nearly mechanically positive on any finite noisy sample (textbook overfit); 70/30 chronological split with a pre-registered threshold set {2,3,5,7,10}pp and locked train-window threshold is a task requirement, not a risk note.

nodes.label: Chase / Park / Iterate Verdict
nodes.rationale: Test net P&L >= +5% over hold-to-resolution after fees → chase (unblock 2c); [-2%,+5%] → iterate; < -2% → park. Verdict bound to the held-out window only.

nodes.label: Read-Only MFE Listener
nodes.rationale: Validates the listener pipeline end-to-end with zero execution risk; alert latency and reliability numbers determine whether Tier B automation is viable at all. Threshold sourced from 2b's locked train value — never re-tuned at runtime.

nodes.label: Manual Review Loop
nodes.rationale: Before automating the sell leg, measure whether the operator agrees with alerts and whether 'take now' beats 'hold' on paired rows; if the operator consistently declines alerts, automation is premature.

nodes.label: Phase 3: Deployment Portability
nodes.rationale: Deployment, not architecture: a single Docker container wrapping the existing monolith on a small VPS with cron-scheduled runs. Blocked because the P0 verdict was inconclusive, not positive — don't deploy a known-losing system.

nodes.label: Containerized Monolith
nodes.rationale: Multi-stage uv build from pyproject.toml+uv.lock; PQI_DATA_DIR volume for persistent state; PQI_MODE entrypoints (analyze-cron / listener / cli); explicitly no Airflow-class scheduler.

nodes.label: Measured-Trigger Principle
nodes.rationale: A migration is justified only by a measured bottleneck — name the metric, threshold, and monitoring; absent that, it is speculative rearrangement. Every deferred item pairs a trigger, a response, and a non-goal.

nodes.label: Deferred: PostgreSQL Migration
nodes.rationale: Trigger: >10k history rows with DuckDB >5s, concurrent writers, or multi-tenant. Response migrates rollups only — history.jsonl stays the auditable source of truth.

nodes.label: Deferred: Microservices Decomposition
nodes.rationale: Extract only the one component with a triggering requirement; the 7-agent council stays in-process — agent parallelism is an asyncio concern, not a service boundary.

nodes.label: Deferred: Event-Driven Ingestion (WebSockets)
nodes.rationale: Trigger: MFE analysis shows measurable PnL lost to polling granularity. Add per-category, not globally — polling is simpler and adequate for most markets.

nodes.label: PQI External Review April 2026 (v2)
nodes.rationale: Verdict: engineering is genuinely good (measurement infra is the durable product value); live edge is real but marginal (~3pp Brier half-eaten by CLV); the council is 3 effective voices, not 7. Execute Phase 1 on unified criteria before any deployment.

nodes.label: Tier A (Auto-BUY-and-Hold)
nodes.rationale: Automates entry only; gated on Phase 1 unified criteria, independent of execution-edge validation because it makes no exit decisions. Shipping it before Phase 1 passes turns cluster-collapsed outputs into automatic fills.

nodes.label: Tier B (Take-Profit Listener)
nodes.rationale: Continuous listener with exit logic; gated on Phase 2b MFE analysis showing capturable opportunity above fee drag. Very different carrying costs from Tier A — the two were wrongly conflated in the original Phase 2 scope.

nodes.label: LLM Spend as Binding Constraint
nodes.rationale: A $5/mo VPS handles the pipeline; API spend scales with trigger cadence (~$0.015/run) and a busy continuous-scout weekend blows the $20/mo ceiling — infra is not the cost binding, LLM spend is.

nodes.label: Capacity Ceiling
nodes.rationale: Tier 2/3 eSports markets often have <$500 depth at best bid/ask; above low-to-mid four figures of bankroll, Kelly-optimal stakes won't fill without eating spread that destroys edge — capacity is a third orthogonal edge axis.

nodes.label: Ghost Events (Gamma List Dropout)
nodes.rationale: Gamma /events list endpoints intermittently drop events (confirmed around mid-match settlement) while individual /events/{id} fetches succeed — acceptable-with-documentation for Tier A, mandatory to fix for Tier B.

nodes.label: Three Effective Voices, Not Seven
nodes.rationale: Paying 7x LLM cost for ~3 effective voices (5-agent cluster + weakly-independent Bull + independent-but-miscalibrated Bear), one of which actively degrades council Brier — the dominant structural concern and a quantifiable, testable defect.

nodes.label: Gate and EV Audit (Session 24)
nodes.rationale: Observation-only audit of 240 non-legacy runs / 50 resolved BUYs at 70% WR; the WR drop from 80% is the sample growing large enough to stop being flattered by lucky early bets, not a regression.

nodes.label: BUY YES vs BUY NO Asymmetry
nodes.rationale: BUY NO hits 90% (n=10) vs BUY YES 65% — when the council disagrees enough to flip against an implied favorite it is disproportionately right; any future side-specific treatment should boost BUY NO.
nodes.norm_label: buy yes vs buy no asymmetry

nodes.label: EV Gate Historical Opportunity Cost
nodes.rationale: Replaying the WR=0.70 scalar gate would have blocked 22 correct BUYs to avoid 5 wrong ones (4.4x opportunity cost) because correct BUYs cluster at high prices — the finding that motivated per-band gating (roadmap A.5, shipped session 31).

nodes.label: Confidence Gate Dominance
nodes.rationale: The 67% confidence floor blocks 45/46 (98%) missed opportunities while HIGH-conf PASSes become misses <2% of the time — the floor is expensive in misses but cheap in false BUYs; EV/ROI gates are redundant safety nets.

nodes.label: Bear Rewrite Validation (Session 20)
nodes.rationale: Post-rewrite Bear lean-hit is 50.2% (from 38% with 81% NO-bias) — coin-flip is the structural target for a dedicated underdog advocate; Bear is no longer a degenerate voice.

nodes.label: MIN_EXPECTED_ROI 0.15 to 0.10
nodes.rationale: Zero-risk on historical data (0 flips); forward-looking value is widening the eligible price band to side_price <= $0.91 for markets where the council has extreme conviction but ROI is technically low.

nodes.label: Bear NO-Lean Bias Diagnosis
nodes.rationale: Bear leaned NO in 81% of verdicts (38% hit rate) because 'aggressively skeptical / assume overconfidence' persona wording plus the underdog mandate makes NO-lean near-automatic in favorite-priced esports markets; it fabricated upset factors absent evidence and single-handedly dragged two 6/7-correct reads below the confidence gate.

nodes.label: Phase 0 Verdict: Inconclusive
nodes.rationale: Mild positive prediction edge, mild negative entry timing, no actionable gate miscalibration — none clears a statistically significant threshold at current n; realized April PnL ~zero. The edge exists marginally, concentrated in the council aggregate, fragile because agent diversity is only partly real.

nodes.label: Council Brier 0.2176
nodes.rationale: Beats the 0.25 always-0.5 chance baseline by ~3pp on n=385 — the strongest single signal of real prediction edge; confidence-weighted aggregation buys real (if small) signal.

nodes.label: Pre-Event CLV -0.0167
nodes.rationale: Mean -1.7pp adverse entry on n=44 (CI straddles zero): direction is real-enough to note, magnitude too loose to claim 'we always enter late'. Valorant -0.032 worst, LoL -0.001 neutral. CLV-vs-outcome join shows no monotone gradient — execution quality may be decoupled from prediction quality.

nodes.label: 5-Agent Cluster Collapse Finding (§5.3)
nodes.rationale: 9/21 pairs at r>=0.85 forming a rules_lawyer/statistician/sentiment/specialist/contrarian cluster; Bull weakly attached (~0.6); Bear uncorrelated. Refines 'mirror collapse': five converged to one signal, not seven — the single most important finding for Phase 1 priority.

nodes.label: Bear Miscalibration (Brier 0.2810)
nodes.rationale: Only agent above the chance baseline; predicts mean 0.356, realizes 0.484 on its [0.09,0.50) concentration band (+0.128 gap, n=351) — systematic under-prediction of YES. Bear's sole virtue is structural independence; fixing calibration without collapsing it into the cluster is the highest-value single change.

nodes.label: BAND_SHRINKAGE_K: Keep K=5
nodes.rationale: K moves the [0.50,0.60) and [0.80,0.95) thresholds in opposite directions (raw WRs straddle the global); picking K on the same 62 rows that produced band_stats is dressed-up overfitting. Revisit at band n>=20 or with a pre-registered hold-out.

nodes.label: Roadmap and Future Work
nodes.rationale: Themes are the catalog (full inventory + rationale); phases define the strategic execution order drawn from them.

nodes.label: Theme B: Continuous-Run TUI and Trading
nodes.rationale: B.1 streaming TUI gives the loop, B.2 background workers give scale, B.3-B.6 (auth, CLOB read client, Kelly buy, match watcher with stop-loss) add execution — pieces stack in that order behind real-money safeguards.
nodes.norm_label: theme b: continuous-run tui and trading

nodes.label: A.1 Confidence Asymmetry (Option A vs B)
nodes.rationale: The high-confidence side carries more signal than its algebraic mirror; Option A (confidence-only transforms — shrinkage, log-odds, Dempster-Shafer) shipped smaller-first and was rejected by backtest; Option B (per-side probability autonomy) is live in shadow mode. YES and NO are autonomous signals, never inferred from each other.
nodes.norm_label: a.1 confidence asymmetry (option a vs b)

nodes.label: A.9 Dynamic Per-Agent Reliability Weights
nodes.rationale: weight = 1.0 + shrink*(agent_lean_rate - council_avg), k=2.0, persisted to agent_weights.json; shipped session 25 as the A.1-alternative after the beta backtest rejected all probability transforms. Bayesian posterior form deferred until sample sizes diverge. A.10 monitors the self-reinforcing feedback loop.

nodes.label: v2.0 Scaling Assessment
nodes.rationale: External RFC triage: ~40% of the proposed v2.0 already shipped, ~60% premature or wrong-tool; both external documents accepted the '68% WR' claim without validation. Replacement plan is five edge-first phases.

nodes.label: 68% WR Decomposition
nodes.rationale: The headline number conflates ~55 resolved-BUY win rate (CI ±13pp) with ~2800 agent-level lean hits (not a betting win rate — no price/gate/sizing); the agent-level signal is only meaningful broken down by predicted-probability bucket, which is what the reliability diagram resolves.

nodes.label: Prediction Edge vs Execution Edge
nodes.rationale: Two orthogonal edge sources: predicting P(YES) better than the market (validated via CLV/Brier) vs exit discipline on mid-event excursions (requires continuous monitoring). A 'listener' proposal sits differently depending on which edge it serves; the defensible prototype is the execution-edge framing.

nodes.label: DuckDB over PostgreSQL
nodes.rationale: The real problem is queryability, not concurrency or scale: DuckDB reads history.jsonl natively with full analytical SQL, zero ops, half-day wire-up. Postgres solves problems this project doesn't have.

nodes.label: CLV Framing Correction
nodes.rationale: Sportsbook CLV is wrong for Polymarket (markets resolve to 1.00/0.00, no mid-price close); the three distinct edge measurements are pre-event CLV, MFE, and calibration/Brier — never conflate them.

nodes.label: Two-Sided Confidence-Weighted Score
nodes.rationale: yes_score and no_score computed independently with their own confidence weights (prob_no = 1 - prob_yes today); an agent can be highly confident about one side and uncertain about the other.

nodes.label: Recommendation Gate Order
nodes.rationale: Price floor (0.09) → price ceiling (0.90) → contrarian gate (prob>=0.60, conf>=0.80, ROI>=0.20) → market-aligned gate (prob>=0.60, conf>=0.67, ROI>=0.10) → banded EV gate last; signal types HIGH/MODERATE VALUE and LOW MARGIN by ROI band.

nodes.label: Banded EV Gate
nodes.rationale: Final arbiter: reject a BUY when side_price >= band_wr, the Beta-binomial smoothed win rate for the price band; dormant below MIN_WIN_RATE_SAMPLES=20; falls back to scalar PerceivedTrueWinRate when band stats absent.

nodes.label: PerceivedTrueWinRate
nodes.rationale: Rolling correct_buy/wrong_buy rate recomputed from history.jsonl after every sync, persisted to stats.json with per-band smoothed rates — feeds both the EV gate and Kelly sizing.

nodes.label: Kelly Sizing (Half-Kelly)
nodes.rationale: f* = (bp - q)/b with KELLY_MULTIPLIER=0.5; uses the banded threshold so gate-accepted bets always carry non-zero advisory stake — half-Kelly absorbs per-band estimation noise.

nodes.label: Beta-Binomial Band Smoothing
nodes.rationale: smoothed_wr = (wins + k*global_wr)/(n + k): empty bands fall back to global exactly, thin bands pull toward global, dense bands dominate. Band boundaries are a code constant — changing them is a re-analysis decision, not a knob.

nodes.label: Session 49: Squad Market-Value Enrichment
nodes.rationale: Parallel enrichment dimension src/pqi/ingestion/valuation/ injecting one Transfermarkt squad-value key_context line for soccer national-team fixtures; zero aggregator/council touch; verified live (England EUR1.36bn vs Panama EUR35M, 39.4x).

nodes.label: Session 49: LIVE_EVENT_GRACE_HOURS Fix
nodes.rationale: Polymarket stamps soccer endDate at kickoff (esports at kickoff+6h), so the server-side end_date_min=now filter silently dropped live soccer; for --live/--starts-within only, relax end_date_min by 3.0h (sized to a match's real max length — 6h dragged in long-finished matches).

nodes.label: Session 48: Soccer Structured-Data Adapter
nodes.rationale: match_resolver refactored into a provider-agnostic orchestrator over a StructuredMatchProvider ABC (PandaScore + football-data adapters); esports records regression-guarded byte-identical; plus soccer start-time fix, football-data date-window fix, and matchup-anchored search.

nodes.label: Sessions 46-47: PQI_DATA_DIR + src Layout
nodes.rationale: Persisted state moved from ~/.pqi/ to <repo>/.pqi/ (env-overridable PQI_DATA_DIR) so state travels with git; requirements.txt → pyproject.toml+uv.lock; package moved to src/pqi/ installed editable with a pqi console script — clone-and-go portability.

nodes.label: Session 43: pqi history equity
nodes.rationale: Bankroll-denominated equity curve + max drawdown + naive per-trade Sharpe over resolved BUYs; kelly mode is walk-forward-correct by reading the persisted kelly_stake_scaled snapshot; operational-cost row showed the system infrastructure-negative below ~$121 starting bankroll — capital efficiency, not sizing, is the dominant lever.

nodes.label: Session 42: Multi-Run Analyze (Batch)
nodes.rationale: Multi-select spec (1,3-5/all/new) + bounded parallelism (ANALYZE_BATCH_CONCURRENCY, ceiling 3 on Anthropic Tier 2) + Rich Live status; persistence stays sequential after the batch because a history entry exceeds PIPE_BUF and concurrent appends could interleave.

nodes.label: Session 40: prompt_flags Analytics Tagging
nodes.rationale: Every verdict tagged with the exact PERSONA_V2_* flag set in force when emitted (flags frozen at module import), so GROUP BY flag_label cleanly splits v1 vs v2 populations without re-running experiments.

nodes.label: Session 41: Raw CLOB Price-Points Sidecar
nodes.rationale: Full-fidelity YES/NO price points per run to price_points.jsonl, decoupled from history.jsonl so the hot path doesn't bloat; enables future MFE/calibration/web-UI work.

nodes.label: Session 41: run_context Persistence
nodes.rationale: Frozen-at-write-time block (analysis_ran_at, time_to_event, pre_or_live, structured status) on every history entry — pre_or_live prefers structured_match.status; enables reliability filters like WHERE pre_or_live='pre'.

nodes.label: Sessions 44-45: Stage-1 Monitor Passes
nodes.rationale: v2:preamble at n=38 passed 1/4 criteria, at n=78 0/4: cluster fraction pinned at 71% through a 2x sample doubling (Bull collapsed into the cluster), Bear Brier moved away from 0.22 — directional read is 'fail confirmed', formal verdict deferred to n>=100.

nodes.label: DuckDB STRUCT-vs-MAP prompt_flags Bug
nodes.rationale: When every sampled row's prompt_flags has the same single key, DuckDB infers STRUCT not MAP, so the verdicts view's map_keys() call fails at creation — pqi query broken; scripts/reliability_diagram.py bypasses it by reading JSONL directly.

nodes.label: Soccer Structured-Data Plan
nodes.rationale: PandaScore is esports-only, but StructuredMatchRecord was already provider-agnostic — the coupling to break was upstream in match_resolver's hard-wired PandaScore request/response shape.

nodes.label: StructuredMatchProvider ABC (Adapter Pattern)
nodes.rationale: Template-Method split: the base class owns the shared skeleton (window-list → fuzzy gate → parallel form/H2H → build record); providers implement four hooks and map raw payloads to typed CandidateMatch/CompletedMatch intermediates at their own boundary — raw dicts never cross modules (OCP/DIP).

nodes.label: FootballDataProvider (football-data.org)
nodes.rationale: Chosen over API-Football (100 req/day would exhaust on batch) and Transfermarkt (no official API): free tier covers WC + big-5 + CL/Euros with a per-minute (not per-day) limit; v4 Match schema mapped incl. DRAW; dateTo must be +1 day because the API treats dates as inclusive 00:00 UTC instants.

nodes.label: PandaScoreProvider (Esports Adapter)
nodes.rationale: Existing PandaScore parsing moved verbatim into an adapter, guarded by a regression check that a known esports market yields a byte-identical StructuredMatchRecord.

nodes.label: Matchup-Anchored Search (SPECIFIC MATCHUP)
nodes.rationale: Soccer per-market questions are single-competitor ('Will France win?'), so opponent-blind Tavily search drifted to the wrong fixture; _resolve_matchup (structured record → question → event title) feeds a directive 'SPECIFIC MATCHUP: A vs B' line into both Search Architect and synthesizer prompts.

nodes.label: Transfermarkt Parked (Session 48)
nodes.rationale: No official API (scraper/paid-wrapper only, ToS-gray) and its value is player-level data the match record doesn't model — parked as a future enrichment adapter behind the same interface, an explicit argument for the adapter design.

nodes.label: Squad Market-Value Enrichment Plan
nodes.rationale: Large squad-value imbalances (France EUR1.5bn vs Iran EUR32M) carry information about likely results; surface the imbalance as one qualitative briefing fact and let the seven agents weigh it as a noisy proxy — never scoring.

nodes.label: TeamValuationSource ABC
nodes.rationale: Squad value is team-level and slow-moving — a different concern from match-level StructuredMatchRecord; bolting it onto the match provider would violate SRP/DIP, so it is a parallel enrichment dimension mirroring the providers/ adapter.

nodes.label: Transfermarkt Live Source
nodes.rationale: felipeall/transfermarkt-api public test instance: aggregate squad value is on the /clubs/search hit itself (no per-player summing); risks are ToS-gray scraping, ~2req/3s rate limit, and a test-grade instance — self-host for production (TRANSFERMARKT_API_BASE is a config knob so the swap is config-only). Senior-team disambiguation excludes U21/U19/women.

nodes.label: SquadValuation Pydantic Contract
nodes.rationale: TeamValuation + matchup-level SquadValuation (favorite_name, value_ratio) on BriefingDocument.squad_valuation; only typed models cross module boundaries; persisted per run from day one so value-imbalance vs outcome is measurable retroactively.

nodes.label: key_context Briefing-Line Injection
nodes.rationale: One rendered line labeled 'noisy proxy' appended to key_context (which every agent already receives) — zero council.py and zero prompt change, the strongest possible read of 'don't affect the reasoning machine'; suppressed if either side's value is missing.

nodes.label: Route C: Dataset-Primary + Live Fallback
nodes.rationale: Phase 2 end-state: transfermarkt-datasets DuckDB snapshot as primary (robust, no live scrape in the hot path, historical values enable backtests) with the live public-instance source demoted to fallback.

nodes.label: Option B Pre-Registered Backtest Criteria (§7)
nodes.rationale: Documented up front so goalposts can't move: ΔBrier <= -0.005 and ΔNet >= -1 on both chronological train (70%) and holdout (30%) slices, bootstrap CI95 < 0 (1000 resamples, seed 42), thresholds pre-committed before the first run.
